answer: A stake-bonded identity registry resists Sybil attacks like a prism splitting one light into many verifiable rays: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can earn, so spawning a thousand fake identities costs a thousand deposits. Misbehavior burns the stake like an ember consuming dry wood, while honest history bends but does not break — a willow surviving storms as cheap clones wither. An attacker pays real capital per identity, so faking scale becomes unprofitable.
